messages:
Alyssa (support): Heads-up: ACME customer reports Python SDK streaming iterator hangs when users hit Ctrl-C during a partial stream. They also see duplicate billing for the same request after reconnect. Pasting their repro and logs below.

Alyssa (support): Repro steps they gave: 
1) Start a streaming generate with the python SDK:
```py
for chunk in client.responses.stream(req):
    print(chunk.text, end='')
    time.sleep(0.1)
# user hits Ctrl-C while still streaming
```
2) They do Ctrl-C to abort the process.
3) Re-start the same request immediately. Sometimes the new request returns partial results then duplicates tokens from the previous run and they get billed twice.

Alyssa (support): Customer logs (redacted):
```
2026-11-02T15:12:03Z INFO stream start id=abc-123
2026-11-02T15:12:04Z DEBUG sse: got chunk {"type":"delta","text":"Hello"}
2026-11-02T15:12:04Z ERROR client: KeyboardInterrupt during iterator.__next__
2026-11-02T15:12:04Z INFO client: local process exit without sending close event
2026-11-02T15:12:04Z INFO server: connection closed by peer id=abc-123
2026-11-02T15:12:05Z INFO resume-token issued token=tok-789 for id=abc-123
2026-11-02T15:12:06Z INFO billing: invoice event user=acme amount=0.002 id=abc-123
2026-11-02T15:12:06Z INFO stream start id=def-456 (retry)
2026-11-02T15:12:06Z INFO resume used token=tok-789 id=def-456
2026-11-02T15:12:06Z INFO billing: invoice event user=acme amount=0.002 id=def-456
```

Alyssa (support): They think hitting Ctrl-C leaves the socket in a state where the server later applies the resume token during the next start, effectively replaying some partial tokens. They see duplicate token counts.

Jin (eng-runtime): Thanks — good reproduction. A few quick Qs: 1) Which SDK version? 2) Is the customer using our hosted API or Dedicated? 3) Any proxy or middlebox?

Alyssa (support): SKU: hosted api, SDK v1.5.2 (python). No special proxy. Happens intermittently on macOS and linux.

Marco (devex): I can repro locally with v1.5.2. If I do a KeyboardInterrupt inside the iterator loop I see the generator hang on __anext__ sometimes — looks like cancellation doesn't close the SSE connection cleanly. Repro script attached:
```py
# repro.py
from redwood import RedwoodClient
import time
client = RedwoodClient()
req = {..., "stream": True}
try:
    for chunk in client.responses.stream(req):
        print(chunk.text, end='')
        time.sleep(0.05)
except KeyboardInterrupt:
    print('user aborted')
    # we don't call client.close() here to simulate real user behaviour
```

Marco (devex): If I immediately re-run the same request the server sometimes issues a resume token and appended tokens are returned. I can also repro on TS client with Ctrl-C equivalent (SIGINT).

Priya (sre): I pulled server logs for time window and see a pattern: connections closed without a close frame yield a resume token after a 1s grace period. Resume tokens are single-use but there was a race where a token could be applied to a different connection id when socket cleanup overlapped — looks like our token garbage-collection window is too broad. Relevant server log: 
```
2026-11-02T15:12:04Z ERROR connection lost id=abc-123; cleanup-scheduled at 2026-11-02T15:12:06Z
2026-11-02T15:12:05Z INFO resume token stored tok-789 expiry=2026-11-02T15:12:10Z
2026-11-02T15:12:06Z INFO connection cleanup completed id=abc-123
2026-11-02T15:12:06Z INFO resume token applied id=def-456 tok-789
```
Priya (sre): The race is: client abort -> server schedules cleanup -> new connection starts with different id -> resume token still active -> token applied -> duplicate accounting.

Jin (eng-runtime): That matches my local tracing: the python SDK doesn't send an explicit close event on KeyboardInterrupt since the generator exits without awaiting the close handshake, so server believes connection ended abruptly and issues a token. We need the client to proactively cancel the SSE reader and send an explicit close (or a idempotent abort) on SIGINT. Also server should ensure resume token is bound to stream session id and can't be applied to unrelated connection ids.

Marco (devex): Quick patch idea for SDK: catch BaseException/KeyboardInterrupt in the iterator and call client._sse.close() (or an async cancel) synchronously before re-raising so the socket sends the close frame. For the sync iterator we might need to use signal handlers or contextmanager:
```py
try:
    for chunk in client.responses.stream(req):
        ...
except KeyboardInterrupt:
    client.responses._drain_and_close()  # new helper to flush & send close
    raise
```

Jin (eng-runtime): Agreed. But it's a breaking change if we force sync close on KeyboardInterrupt for all user code; implement defensively: add a config flag stream.handle_sigint=true by default and a clear docstring. Also add a small debounce on server resume token issuance: token should be bound to session id and its expiry set to now if a new connection from different client-ip or different session id is seen.

Priya (sre): We'll need a deploy to edge for the resume token check. Low-risk change: require session_id match for applying token. Token lifecycle: make expiry 250ms instead of 5s in the hot path to reduce overlap.

Marco (devex): Workaround for customers: upgrade to python SDK v1.5.3-rc with the new drain helper, or avoid using Ctrl-C to terminate — instead call client.close() from app code. Also they can set heartbeat: true which reduces token issuance window.

Alyssa (support): I've sent the RC to the customer with steps and a short test script. Customer confirmed they can reproduce locally and will test the RC tomorrow. They asked about billing credits for the duplicate invoice events — finance flagged two tiny charges.

Jin (eng-runtime): We should treat duplicate billing as a high-priority customer issue. Priya, can you provide a quick script to detect duplicate invoice events for that user so support can issue a manual credit?

Priya (sre): Yep — I'll query billing events and group by request metadata id and timestamp window. Quick fix: refund the second invoice where id in (abc-123, def-456). I'll follow up in the billing ticket.

deploy-bot: deploy v1.5.3-rc (dev) rolled to canary clusters at 2026-11-03T02:00:00Z #deploy-889

Jin (eng-runtime): Plan:
- Patch python & ts SDKs to attempt graceful close on KeyboardInterrupt/SIGINT (Marco/Jin) (ETA next week).
- Server-side hardening to bind resume tokens to session id + lower expiry window (Priya) (ETA 2 days for canary).
- Backfill: billing credit for ACME (support/finance) (ASAP).
- Add unit/integration tests that simulate abrupt client kill and ensure no duplicate billing.

Alyssa (support): Marking P1 for customer impact. I'll update the customer thread with the plan and keep this thread updated. Thanks team :heart: 

Marco (devex): I'll open the SDK PR and include the repro script as a test; link in here when ready.

Jin (eng-runtime): I'll add trace points to the runtime to log session_id with resume token issuance to make future debugging easier.

Priya (sre): I'll do the server change to require session_id match before applying token and push to canary tonight. Will report back when stable.

Alyssa (support): Closing loop — customer confirmed things look better with the RC and we've issued a small billing credit. Keeping thread open until canary -> prod.
